title: Share of the Month Charged on Late Microsoft 365 Annual Invoices: Pro Rata and Catch-Up
content:
On a Microsoft 365 Cloud Subscriptions (CSP) annual cycle invoice, the share of the month that the late charge covers depends on how late the invoice is.

**Days past due.** The invoice's days past due are the calendar days from its posting date to the assessment date, less the plan's net payment terms in days.

**Share of the month.**

- **Pro rata.** An invoice 30 or fewer days past due is charged pro rata: the month's charge times its days past due, divided by 30.
- **Catch-up.** An invoice more than 60 days past due that carries no late charge yet is caught up: the month's charge times the whole 30-day periods it has been past due.
- **Neither.** Any other invoice is charged neither a pro-rata share nor a catch-up. This covers an invoice 31 to 60 days past due, and one more than 60 days past due that already carries a late charge.

The posting date and any late charge already on the invoice are read from the subscription's billing ledger.

## Boundary table

| Days past due | Late charge already on the invoice | Share of the month's charge |
|---|---|---|
| 18 | — | 18 divided by 30 |
| 30 | — | 30 divided by 30 |
| 31 | — | neither pro rata nor catch-up |
| 60 | — | neither pro rata nor catch-up |
| 61 | none | 2 whole 30-day periods |
| 61 | one or more | neither pro rata nor catch-up |
| 95 | none | 3 whole 30-day periods |

## Hypothetical illustration (net terms of 30 days)

An annual invoice is posted on 1 January and assessed on 1 March. That is 59 calendar days, so it is 29 days past due. With a month's charge of 90.00 USD, the share is 90.00 times 29, divided by 30, which is 87.00.

An invoice assessed 100 days past due with no late charge on it yet has 3 whole 30-day periods. The same month's charge gives 270.00.
